overall: The AG found the Barre Select Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law as alleged: meetings were accessible, the notice amendments were permissible, and the former Town Administrator's name was not a violation. Bylaw and pre-30-day historical claims were declined.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the June 13 and June 20 Friday meetings in the Henry Woods Building were inaccessible because the building is generally closed to the public on Fridays.
allegations.key_passage: To the extent the complaint alleges that the complainant was unable to access the June 13 executive session, we find no violation where a public body may exclude the public from a properly held executive session.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board amended its June 16 meeting notices within 48 hours to add votes on Town Meeting warrant articles and override ballot language.
allegations.key_passage: For the reasons explained above, we find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law when, on June 16, it amended the notices for its June 16 meetings.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the June 13 notice wrongly listed a former Town Administrator, misleading the public about responsibility for the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: First, the Open Meeting Law does not require that the Town Administrator be listed on meeting notices.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board violated Town bylaws by failing to broadcast its meetings.
allegations.key_passage: we would decline to review an allegation that a public body failed to comply with Town bylaws where, even if true, such an allegation would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant submitted a 151-page historical record claiming a multi-year pattern of short-notice and same-day agenda changes.
allegations.key_passage: Our office does not perform broad audits of public bodies nor can we review alleged violations of the Open Meeting Law that occurred, or were reasonably discoverable, more than 30 days prior to a complaint being filed with the public body.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
